recommended_model.rationale: The 'order_items' table serves as the central fact table as it contains transactional data related to each order, including price and freight value. The dimension tables provide context such as customer details, product information, seller data, payment methods, and customer reviews, enabling comprehensive analysis of sales performance.

quality_findings: The 'geolocation' table has 261831 duplicate rows, which may lead to inaccurate geolocation data.
The 'order_reviews' table has a high percentage of null values (88.34%) in the 'review_comment_title' column, indicating potential data collection issues.
The 'order_payments' table has outliers in 'payment_installments' (6313 distinct values), which may skew financial analysis.
data_science_opportunities: Churn prediction could be implemented by analyzing customer purchase patterns and review scores.
Demand forecasting can be enhanced by utilizing historical sales data from the 'order_items' table along with seasonal trends.
Customer segmentation analysis could be conducted to tailor marketing strategies based on purchasing behavior and demographics.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(price) AS REAL) AS total_revenue FROM order_items;
kpis.why_it_matters: Total revenue is a key indicator of business performance, reflecting overall sales success.

kpis.name: Average Order Value
kpis.sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(price) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS average_order_value FROM order_items;
kpis.why_it_matters: Average order value helps assess customer spending behavior and can guide pricing strategies.

kpis.name: Revenue by Product Category
kpis.sql: SELECT p.product_category_name, CAST(SUM(oi.price) AS REAL) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_category_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: Understanding revenue by product category helps identify top-performing categories and informs inventory and marketing strategies.

kpis.name: Orders by Payment Type
kpis.sql: SELECT op.payment_type, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM order_payments op JOIN orders o ON op.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY op.payment_type ORDER BY total_orders DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: Analyzing orders by payment type reveals customer preferences and can influence payment processing strategies.

kpis.name: Average Review Score
kpis.sql: SELECT CAST(AVG(review_score) AS REAL) AS average_review_score FROM order_reviews;
kpis.why_it_matters: Average review score is crucial for assessing customer satisfaction and product quality.

kpis.name: Top 10 Cities by Customer Count
kpis.sql: SELECT customer_city, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY customer_city ORDER BY customer_count DESC LIMIT 10;
kpis.why_it_matters: Identifying top cities by customer count can help target marketing efforts and optimize logistics.

insights: Total revenue for the period is approximately $13.6 million, indicating strong sales performance and overall business health.
The average order value is around $137.75, which suggests that customers are spending a healthy amount per transaction; this insight can help refine pricing strategies.
The top product category is 'beleza_saude' with over $1.25 million in revenue, highlighting a key area for inventory focus and marketing efforts.
Most orders are paid for using credit cards, accounting for 76,505 transactions; understanding this preference can enhance payment processing strategies.

The average review score is 4.09, reflecting generally high customer satisfaction, but the high percentage of null values in review comments (88.34%) raises concerns about the completeness of feedback, potentially impacting product improvement efforts.
There are 261,831 duplicate rows in the geolocation data, which could lead to inaccuracies in customer location insights, affecting targeted marketing and logistics planning.
